Inventions are directed to components, subassemblies, systems, and/or methods for continuously variable transmissions (CVT). In one aspect, a control system is adapted to facilitate a change in the ratio of a CVT. A control system includes a control reference nut coupled to a feedback cam and operably coupled to a skew cam. In some cases, the skew cam is configured to interact with carrier plates of a CVT. Various inventive feedback cams and skew cams can be used to facilitate shifting the ratio of a CVT. In some transmissions described, the planet subassemblies include legs configured to cooperate with the carrier plates. In some cases, a neutralizer assembly is operably coupled to the carrier plates. A shift cam and a traction sun are adapted to cooperate with other components of the CVT to support operation and/or functionality of the CVT. Among other things, shift control interfaces for a CVT are described.

The inventions relate to components, subassemblies, systems, and methods for continuously variable transmissions (CVTs). In particular, they describe mechanisms for controlling and facilitating changes in the transmission ratio. A control system may use a control reference nut coupled to a feedback cam and operably connected to a skew cam, enabling coordinated adjustment of the CVT ratio.

The CVT may incorporate feedback cams and skew cams that work together to produce ratio shifts. In some configurations, the skew cams interact with carrier plates to control the position or orientation of transmission elements. Planet subassemblies may include legs that cooperate with these carrier plates, while a neutralizer assembly may also be coupled to the plates to support neutral positioning or related control functions.

Additional components, including shift cams, traction suns, and shift control interfaces, may further support CVT operation. Together, these elements provide coordinated mechanical and control functions for adjusting, maintaining, and managing the transmission ratio across the CVT’s operating range.
outputs.L4:
The inventions relate to control systems for continuously variable transmissions (CVTs), particularly mechanisms for controlling transmission ratio and coordinating shifting operations. The systems integrate mechanical control elements—including a reference nut, feedback cam, skew cam, carrier plates, planet subassemblies, a neutralizer assembly, shift cam, and traction sun—to provide accurate and responsive adjustment of the transmission.

In one aspect, the reference nut establishes or communicates a desired ratio setting. The feedback cam indicates the transmission’s current operating condition, while the skew cam converts the difference between the commanded and actual conditions into controlled movement of the carrier plates. Movement of the carrier plates adjusts the orientation or operating position of the planet subassemblies, thereby changing their engagement with the traction sun and other traction surfaces. This coordinated action alters the effective transmission ratio in a continuous and controlled manner.

The feedback arrangement allows the transmission to monitor its response to a ratio command and progressively reduce the correcting input as the desired ratio is reached. Such closed-loop mechanical interaction can limit overshoot, abrupt movement, and unnecessary loading of the transmission components. It also helps maintain the selected ratio despite variations in speed, torque, or other operating conditions.

The inventions further incorporate a neutralizer assembly and shift cam to coordinate ratio control with neutral or shifting functions. The neutralizer assembly can selectively modify or interrupt the normal control relationship when a neutral condition or another designated operating mode is required. The shift cam provides an interface through which a control input is translated into coordinated movement of the relevant transmission components. Together, these elements support controlled transitions among operating states while preserving proper alignment and engagement of the traction and planetary components.

By combining command, feedback, actuation, and neutralizing functions in an integrated mechanical control architecture, the inventions enable smoother and more effective CVT ratio changes. The resulting systems can improve shift quality, responsiveness, stability, component coordination, and overall transmission functionality across a range of operating conditions.
outputs.L5:
## Inventions: The CVT and Its Various Applications

Among the many **inventions** that have transformed modern transportation, the **CVT**, or continuously variable transmission, stands out for its innovative design. Unlike a conventional automatic transmission with fixed gears, a CVT can move smoothly through a wide range of gear ratios. This allows an engine to operate at an efficient speed while the vehicle accelerates without noticeable gear changes.

The basic idea behind the CVT has existed for centuries, with early concepts appearing in sketches by Leonardo da Vinci. Over time, engineers developed various CVT systems using belts, pulleys, chains, rollers, and electronic controls. Today, these transmissions are commonly found in cars, scooters, snowmobiles, agricultural machinery, and industrial equipment.

CVTs offer various advantages, including smooth acceleration, improved fuel efficiency, and simplified operation. However, they may also produce unfamiliar engine sounds and require specialized maintenance. As technology continues to advance, new CVT inventions may make these systems stronger, quieter, and suitable for an even wider range of vehicles and machines.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing inventions related to control systems, feedback cams, skew cams, carrier plates, and shift interfaces for continuously variable transmissions.
counterfactuals.output: A control system for a continuously variable transmission is disclosed. The system includes a carrier plate supporting a plurality of ratio-control elements and a feedback cam operatively coupled to a movable transmission member. The feedback cam provides a mechanical indication of an actual transmission ratio and cooperates with a control input to regulate movement of the ratio-control elements. A skew cam is configured to convert relative rotational or translational movement into coordinated angular displacement of one or more transmission components, thereby adjusting the transmission ratio while maintaining desired traction, clamping, or alignment conditions. The carrier plate includes guide features, cam followers, and interfaces arranged to distribute control forces and constrain movement along predetermined paths. A shift interface, which may be mechanically, electrically, hydraulically, or electromechanically actuated, receives a commanded ratio and applies a corresponding input to the feedback cam, skew cam, or carrier plate. Difference between the commanded ratio and the actual ratio produces corrective movement until a selected operating condition is achieved. In certain embodiments, the cams include nonlinear profiles that compensate for transmission geometry, load, speed, or actuator characteristics. The disclosed arrangements provide compact ratio control, inherent mechanical feedback, reduced actuator demand, and improved shift accuracy and stability across a continuously variable operating range.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a CVT patent covering ratio-changing mechanisms, including a control reference nut coupled to a feedback cam and operably connected to a skew cam.
counterfactuals.output:
The patent describes a control system for changing the ratio of a continuously variable transmission (CVT), particularly a traction-type CVT using tiltable rotating elements.

Its key components are:

- **Skew cam:** Applies a controlled skew to the transmission’s traction elements, causing their rotational axes to tilt and thereby changing the speed ratio.
- **Control reference nut:** Represents the commanded or target ratio and converts control input—typically rotary motion—into an axial reference position.
- **Feedback cam:** Coupled to the control reference nut and responsive to the transmission’s actual tilt or ratio position.
- **Closed-loop mechanical control:** The reference nut and feedback cam compare the requested ratio with the current ratio. Their relative displacement operates the skew cam, which produces corrective skew until the actual position approaches the commanded position.

In effect, the arrangement provides mechanical servo control of the CVT ratio: an operator or actuator selects a desired ratio, the skew cam initiates the ratio change, and feedback progressively removes the skew as the transmission reaches the target. This can improve ratio accuracy, stability, and shift smoothness while reducing the need for direct electronic sensing or continuous actuator force.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise technical overview of continuously variable transmission components and methods, mentioning planet subassembly legs, a neutralizer assembly, a shift cam, and a traction sun.
counterfactuals.output:
A continuously variable transmission (CVT) may use a traction-type planetary variator to provide stepless ratio control. The variator includes a **traction sun**, input and output traction rings, and multiple planet subassemblies arranged around the transmission axis. Each planet subassembly has a traction planet supported by **planet subassembly legs**, which locate the planet and permit controlled tilting of its rotational axis.

A **shift cam** converts actuator movement into coordinated displacement of the planet subassembly legs. This changes the planets’ tilt angle and the effective rolling radii at their traction contacts, thereby varying the transmission ratio continuously. A **neutralizer assembly** selectively unloads, separates, or repositions the traction elements so that torque transfer is substantially interrupted without requiring the prime mover to stop.

Typical operating methods include applying clamping force to establish traction contact, actuating the shift cam to set the desired ratio, synchronizing planet tilt across the assembly, and operating the neutralizer assembly during neutral selection, starting, stopping, or fault conditions. Lubrication, preload, and closed-loop actuator control are used to limit slip, wear, and thermal loading.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an invention disclosure paragraph for a CVT ratio-control system in which skew cams interact with carrier plates and feedback cams facilitate transmission shifting.
counterfactuals.output: A continuously variable transmission (CVT) ratio-control system is disclosed in which one or more skew cams cooperate with respective carrier plates to vary the angular or axial disposition of transmission traction elements and thereby establish a commanded transmission ratio. Each skew cam includes a contoured cam surface configured to convert rotational or linear actuator input into controlled displacement of the associated carrier plate. One or more feedback cams are operatively coupled to the carrier plates or to a ratio-responsive transmission member and provide mechanical position feedback representative of the actual transmission ratio. During shifting, the feedback cams modify, balance, or oppose the actuator input such that movement of the skew cams is progressively reduced as the carrier plates approach positions corresponding to the commanded ratio. The resulting closed-loop mechanical interaction facilitates smooth, stable transmission shifting, limits overshoot, and permits accurate ratio control under varying speed and load conditions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: In formal patent language, describe several related innovations for CVT subassemblies, shift controls, carrier plates, cams, and traction components.
counterfactuals.output:
The following exemplary disclosure describes a family of related innovations applicable to continuously variable transmissions (“CVTs”), including toroidal, traction-drive, variable-radius, and other ratio-varying transmission architectures.

### CVT Subassembly

In one aspect, a continuously variable transmission subassembly comprises a support structure, an input member rotatable about a transmission axis, an output member, and a plurality of traction elements disposed between respective traction surfaces of the input and output members. Each traction element may be supported for rotation about a traction-element axis and for controlled tilting about a steering axis. Variation of the angular orientation of the traction elements changes respective effective contact radii and thereby varies a transmission ratio between the input and output members.

The subassembly may be configured as a preassembled cartridge removably receivable within a transmission housing. The cartridge may include one or more carrier plates, traction-element supports, reaction members, bearings, lubrication passages, and shift-actuation interfaces. Locating features formed on the cartridge may cooperate with complementary housing features to establish concentricity and axial position without requiring individual alignment of the traction elements during final assembly.

In certain embodiments, the support structure includes a first carrier plate and a second carrier plate coupled by circumferentially distributed spacers. The spacing between the carrier plates may be selectively adjustable to establish traction-element preload. One or more resilient members may maintain the preload despite thermal expansion, component wear, or dimensional tolerance variation.

### Shift-Control Assembly

In another aspect, a shift-control assembly comprises a control member movable in response to an operator command or an electronic control signal, a plurality of shift links operatively coupled to respective traction-element supports, and a synchronizing mechanism configured to coordinate movement of the shift links. The synchronizing mechanism causes the traction elements to assume corresponding steering orientations while permitting limited differential movement sufficient to accommodate load distribution and manufacturing variation.

The control member may comprise a rotatable shift ring, an axially movable sleeve, or a combined rotary-and-axial actuator. A plurality of guide formations formed in or coupled to the control member engage follower members associated with the traction-element supports. Movement of the control member causes the follower members to travel along predetermined paths, thereby producing controlled tilting of the traction elements.

A controller may determine a commanded ratio based on one or more of input speed, output speed, torque demand, traction temperature, lubricant condition, vehicle speed, and available normal force. The controller may regulate an electromechanical, hydraulic, or pneumatic actuator to position the control member. Position sensors may directly or indirectly detect the orientations of the control member and the traction elements. The controller may detect a disagreement between commanded and measured positions and responsively limit transmitted torque, increase clamping force, or place the transmission in a predetermined fail-safe ratio.

### Carrier Plate

In a further aspect, a carrier plate for a CVT comprises a generally annular body having a central opening, a plurality of circumferentially spaced support regions, and respective guide structures associated with the support regions. Each guide structure receives a traction-element support or a shift follower and constrains the received component to a prescribed path.

The carrier plate may be manufactured as a unitary plate, a laminated structure, or an assembly of a primary plate and replaceable guide inserts. The guide inserts may be formed from a material having greater wear resistance or lower friction than the primary plate. Indexing features may prevent incorrect circumferential or axial installation of the inserts.

Lubrication channels may be formed within or along a surface of the carrier plate. The channels may deliver lubricant to traction contacts, bearings, cam-follower interfaces, and shift-link pivots. In certain embodiments, the carrier plate includes metering restrictions configured to distribute lubricant according to operating load or rotational speed. A collection channel may recover lubricant discharged from the traction contacts and direct the lubricant toward a sump or heat exchanger.

The carrier plate may further include compliant support regions positioned between a rigid mounting portion and the guide structures. The compliant support regions permit limited movement of the traction elements under transient loading while maintaining predetermined kinematic relationships during ratio adjustment.

### Cam and Follower Arrangement

In another aspect, a cam assembly comprises at least one cam surface and a plurality of followers operatively associated with respective traction elements. The cam surface defines a nonlinear profile selected to provide a desired relationship between actuator displacement and transmission ratio. The profile may provide relatively high positioning resolution near a neutral or commonly used ratio and relatively rapid ratio change near one or both ends of the ratio range.

The cam surface may include a primary shifting portion, a dwell portion, and an overload-release portion. The dwell portion resists unintended ratio change caused by vibration or traction reaction forces. The overload-release portion permits limited follower displacement when a reaction load exceeds a threshold, thereby reducing the likelihood of damage to the shift mechanism.

In certain embodiments, the cam is axially biased against the followers by a spring or hydraulic pressure. A torque-sensitive mechanism modifies the axial bias according to transmitted torque. The resulting follower force may increase under high-load conditions and decrease under low-load conditions, reducing actuation losses while maintaining shift stability.

A replaceable cam insert may define at least part of the cam surface. Different inserts may provide different ratio schedules, actuator-force characteristics, or end-stop positions while permitting use of a common carrier plate and actuator.

### Traction Components

In a further aspect, a traction component comprises a body having a rotational axis and an annular traction surface configured to engage a complementary traction surface through an elastohydrodynamic traction-fluid film. The traction surface may have a crowned, tapered, toroidal, or compound-curvature profile selected to control contact stress and reduce edge loading throughout a range of steering orientations.

The traction component may include a high-strength core and a wear-resistant surface layer. The surface layer may be formed by carburizing, nitriding, physical vapor deposition, chemical vapor deposition, thermal spraying, or another surface-treatment process. Surface texture may be controlled to retain traction fluid while limiting asperity interaction.

Internal passages may conduct lubricant or coolant through the traction component. One or more outlet passages may discharge fluid adjacent to an entering side of a traction contact. In certain embodiments, centrifugal pressure generated by rotation of the component assists fluid delivery without requiring a dedicated pump.

The traction component may be mounted on a support shaft by a bearing arrangement permitting rotation about the traction-element axis and controlled pivoting about the steering axis. A preload member may remove bearing clearance while accommodating differential thermal expansion. A replaceable wear sleeve may be positioned between the support shaft and the bearing arrangement to facilitate servicing.

### Integrated Operation

During operation, torque is transferred from the input member to the traction elements and from the traction elements to the output member through traction contacts maintained under a commanded normal force. To change the transmission ratio, the shift-control assembly moves the followers along the cam surfaces. The resulting movement changes the steering orientations of the traction elements, causing the traction contacts to migrate to different effective radii.

The carrier plates maintain the relative positions of the traction elements, react shifting loads, and distribute lubricant. The compliant and synchronizing features permit the traction elements to self-equalize under load without materially departing from the commanded ratio. The modular construction permits removal and replacement of the CVT subassembly as a unit and allows cam profiles, traction components, and control actuators to be adapted for different operating requirements while retaining a common transmission architecture.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
